decisions.decision: Serve predictions locally on each line
decisions.context: Cameras need defect predictions while devices may have no network access. The design space offers local, distributed and batch serving options (d:5).
decisions.rationale: Offline inference decides the choice: a local service can run without network access. This gives up centralized serving and adds local deployment upkeep.
consequences: Package the model with a local prediction endpoint.
Manage model copies on production devices.

decisions.context: Newly labeled images arrive for weekly retraining; the brief does not call for learning during production inference. The design space distinguishes batch and incremental learning (d:19).

alternatives.label: Batch-based learning
cons: Weekly retraining: waits for next run

alternatives.label: Incremental learning
pros: Weekly retraining: can incorporate data continuously

decisions.rationale: Weekly retraining decides the choice: batch learning fits the stated cadence and avoids continuous-training complexity. New labels wait for the next run.
consequences: Schedule a training run each week.
Validate each trained model before release.

decisions.decision: Automate model building, evaluation and validation
decisions.context: Weekly retraining needs a repeatable path from labeled images to a candidate model. The design space includes an automated model-building pipeline and development-tool training (d:18).

alternatives.label: Model building pipeline
cons: Small team: pipeline setup and upkeep

decisions.rationale: Weekly retraining decides the choice: an automated pipeline makes the weekly process repeatable. The team takes on initial setup and maintenance.
consequences: Represent training, evaluation and validation as pipeline steps.
Keep pipeline operation proportionate to the small team.

decisions.context: The brief explicitly sets a weekly retraining cadence from newly labeled images. The design space includes scheduled and new-data triggers (d:12).

alternatives.label: On-schedule trigger
cons: Weekly retraining: may wait for new labels

alternatives.label: On availability of new training data trigger
pros: Weekly retraining: reacts when labels arrive
cons: Small team: needs reliable data event handling

decisions.rationale: The stated weekly cadence decides the choice: a schedule is simple and predictable. It can wait until the next run when labels arrive just after a run.
consequences: Configure the schedule for weekly execution.
Ensure each run uses the latest available labeled images.

decisions.context: Models are retrained from changing labeled images, so the training input should be identifiable for later review. The design space offers a data version repository and no data versioning (d:11).

alternatives.label: No data versioning
pros: Cost: no versioning service to operate

decisions.rationale: Weekly retraining decides the choice: identifying each training dataset supports repeatable model builds. The team accepts the added repository overhead despite the tight budget.
consequences: Record the dataset version used for each model build.
Budget for storage and maintenance of data versions.

decisions.context: A model trained centrally must be pushed to devices that may be offline. The design space covers automated integration and delivery approaches (d:8).

alternatives.label: CI/CD pipeline
cons: Offline inference: device rollout still needs connectivity or staging

decisions.rationale: Weekly retraining and team size decide the choice: a CI/CD pipeline can make model releases repeatable. Offline devices still require a separate rollout path for periods without connectivity.
consequences: Automate model packaging and release checks.
Provide a mechanism to stage releases for disconnected devices.

decisions.decision: Retain a previous model for rollback
decisions.context: A new model is pushed to production devices after retraining, and the brief gives no guarantee of network access during recovery. The design space includes rollback to a previous version (d:10).

alternatives.label: Rollback to previous model version
cons: Small team and tight budget: retains model copies

alternatives.label: Single model in production
cons: Offline inference: no local fallback model

decisions.rationale: Offline inference decides the choice: keeping a previous model available allows local recovery if a release fails. This costs device storage and rollout handling.
consequences: Keep the previous model available on each device.

decisions.decision: Test trained model quality before release
decisions.context: Weekly retraining produces new candidates for deployment, so a quality gate is needed before replacing the current model. The design space lists trained-model quality testing (d:26).

alternatives.label: Testing trained model quality
cons: Small team: requires evaluation data and review effort

alternatives.label: No testing
cons: Offline inference: poor model may persist until next rollout

decisions.rationale: Offline inference decides the choice: once a poor model reaches a disconnected device, recovery may be delayed. Quality testing adds evaluation work before deployment.
consequences: Set a quality acceptance criterion for each candidate.
Keep evaluation data representative of production defects.

uncovered: How devices receive staged model updates while offline and reconcile when connectivity returns.
Device identity, update authentication and model integrity protection.
Target latency, camera throughput, device hardware and storage limits.
How production predictions and defect labels are collected for monitoring and future training.
